title: Azure Landing Zone Factory — Configuration Contract
description: The single contract read by the wizard (site/), the renderer (factory/renderer/), the bootstrap broker, the scaffold builder, and every generated Terraform layer. Any key emitted by the wizard that is not declared here is a build-breaking error; any Terraform variable in factory/templates/**/variables.tf with no corresponding key here is likewise an error. This bidirectional check is what prevents the wizard/Terraform drift recorded in TODO.md.

azureRegion.description: Azure region short name, e.g. southcentralus. Lowercase, no spaces.

regionCode.description: Abbreviation used in resource names, e.g. scus for southcentralus.

guidOrEmpty.description: A subscription GUID, or empty string meaning 'not yet provisioned / reuse another subscription'.

phone.description: Optional. Used only in generated runbook contact tables. Never transmitted.

schemaVersion.description: Version of THIS schema. The renderer refuses configs whose schemaVersion it does not implement. 4.1.0: finops.defaultSubscriptionBudget — the first budget the factory DEPLOYS rather than documents. It assigns the pinned ALZ library's own Deploy-Budget policy (a DeployIfNotExists the library ships and assigns nowhere) at one management group, giving every subscription beneath it a budget, now and as subscriptions are added later. Additive: absent or enabled=false renders exactly as 4.0.0 did. Note the shape does NOT mirror finops.budgets, because the policy does not: Deploy-Budget takes exactly two thresholds and a single management-group scope, where finops.budgets carries a threshold array and a free-text scope. finops.budgets stays documented-only. Enabling this pins the estate to a local architecture definition even under caf-standard, because the architecture is what binds the override archetype carrying the assignment to the group (decision 0026). 4.0.0 (BREAKING), two changes that both had to be majors and so land together: (1) azure.managementGroups.strategy 'caf-minimal' now deploys a DIFFERENT hierarchy from 'caf-standard' instead of the identical one — it drops Sandbox and Decommissioned, emits its own architecture definition, and refuses a config that also sets azure.subscriptions.sandbox, because that subscription would have nowhere to be placed (guard G31). A 3.x config selecting caf-minimal deployed the full hierarchy and will now deploy ten groups rather than twelve. (2) The six governance.policyBaseline booleans (enforceAllowedLocations, enforceTlsMinimum, enforceNsgOnSubnets, denyPublicIpOnNics, enforceDiagnosticSettings, enforceEncryptionAtRest) are REMOVED. They predate the ALZ policy surface and asked the same questions as the Policies step, with only the Policies step connected to anything. enforcementMode and requiredTags are unaffected and still consumed. 3.2.0: per-subscription brownfield dispositions — an existing subscription is either placed into the new hierarchy now, against a typed acknowledgement, or deferred with onboarding instructions generated for it (ADR 0018 amended). Additive. 3.1.0: a second state backend — HCP Terraform for STATE ONLY, execution stays in GitHub Actions (decision 0023, partially reversing 0015). Additive: backend.type widens to an enum that still defaults to azurerm. 3.0.0 (BREAKING): azure.managementGroups.customHierarchy changed from a free-form flat list of {id, displayName, parentId} into a map of renames keyed by the pinned ALZ library's own management-group ids. The old shape let a client describe a tree the factory never built — it had zero readers — and re-nesting a group changes which archetype, and so which policy set, it inherits. Names are now honoured; structure is the library's. Also adds azure.managementGroups.workloadPlacement. 2.2.0: subscription vending (azure.subscriptions.mode=create with plannedNames, ADR 0020), brownfield redefined as exclude-and-create (ADR 0018), state-storage private-endpoint flag (ADR 0019).

factoryVersion.description: Copied from factory-version.json at generation time. Stamped into the generated repo so upgrade-check can diff.

generatedAt.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of wizard export.

companyName.description: Display name. Used in docs and report headers only.

companyShortName.description: Lowercase alphanumeric, 2-10 chars. This becomes org_prefix in Terraform and the leading token in every resource name, so it is length-constrained by Azure storage-account naming (24 chars total).

outputDirectoryName.description: Folder created under generated-output/. Defaults to companyShortName if omitted.

allowedLocations.description: Enforced by the allowed-locations Azure Policy. Must include primaryRegion and drRegion.

subscriptions.description: Maps 1:1 onto the *_subscription_id variables in terraform/live/*/variables.tf. Empty string means not-yet-provisioned (mode=create, before New-LzSubscriptions.ps1 runs) or slot-not-used. Render guard G25 refuses to render while a required slot is empty, so an unfilled create-mode config can never produce a repository.

mode.description: create: the wizard plans subscription NAMES from the naming convention and scripts/New-LzSubscriptions.ps1 creates them (EA/MCA alias API, manual fallback) and patches the IDs back into this file. existing: IDs are pasted directly (pre-provisioned subscriptions).

plannedNames.description: Convention-derived display names for subscriptions to be created (mode=create). Written by the wizard; consumed by New-LzSubscriptions.ps1. Keys mirror the ID slots.

rootId.description: Management group ID the hierarchy is rooted under. Use the tenant ID to root at Tenant Root Group; use an existing intermediate MG ID to avoid requiring tenant-root write (see assumption A7).

strategy.description: caf-standard: Platform (Identity/Management/Connectivity) + Landing Zones (Corp/Online) + Sandbox + Decommissioned. caf-minimal: Platform + Landing Zones only. custom: hierarchy supplied in customHierarchy.

customHierarchy.description: Required when strategy=custom. Renames of the management groups the pinned ALZ library architecture defines, keyed by the library's own id (alz, platform, landingzones, corp, online, sandbox, decommissioned, management, connectivity, identity, ...). Only names change. The parent edges and the archetype each group carries stay exactly as the library declares them, because re-nesting a group changes which archetype it inherits and therefore which policy set applies to everything beneath it — a decision that cannot be corrected later, since management-group IDs are immutable in Azure. An entry that renames nothing is stripped from the export. Keys are validated against the generated catalog by the wizard and by render guard G29, not by this schema, because the id set belongs to the pinned library rather than to the contract.

id.description: Management-group ID to create instead of the library id. Immutable once applied.

displayName.description: Display name to create instead of the library display name. Changeable later, unlike the ID.

workloadPlacement.description: Which landing-zone management group the workload subscriptions are placed under. This does NOT change how many policy assignments they inherit, which is the usual misreading: online carries none of its own and inherits landingzones' plus the root's either way. What it buys is the ability to differentiate corp from online later without moving the subscription, since corp adds five deny-style assignments that online does not. Placing directly at landingzones forecloses that distinction.

ownershipModel.description: Drives which control set the broker can configure. See risk GH1: personal accounts on the Free plan cannot use environments or branch protection on private repos, so the broker degrades and reports the reduced control set rather than skipping silently.

ownerName.description: GitHub user or org login. Combined with repositoryName to form the OIDC subject claim.

enterpriseSlug.description: Required when ownershipModel=enterprise. Used for enterprise-level Actions policy discovery.

visibility.description: Public is deliberately not permitted. OIDC subject claims and MG topology must not be world-readable (assumption A3).

useSelfHostedRunners.description: v1 emits GitHub-hosted runners only (decision D6). Discovery reports self-hosted runners; setting this true is currently rejected by the renderer with a documented extension point.

backend.description: Where Terraform state lives. Two backends are supported: azurerm (the default — a storage account this factory creates and hardens) and hcp-terraform (HCP Terraform holds the state; GitHub Actions still runs Terraform). Decision 0023 explains why HCP Terraform is state-only: the emitted destroy gates are built on a saved plan file, and TFC remote execution does not support terraform plan -out, so remote execution would silently delete that gate from both workflows.

type.description: Selects the state backend, and with it which broker steps run and which backend template is emitted.

storageAccountName.description: Globally unique, lowercase alphanumeric, max 24 chars.

enabled.description: Emit the state-hardening overlay (private endpoint into the hub + privatelink.blob zone group + gated public-access flip workflow). Requires hub-spoke topology, centralized private DNS, and self-hosted runners in the VNet (ADR 0019); guard G27 refuses otherwise. Day-0 state posture is public endpoint + AAD-only regardless (WAF-validated: IP allowlists cannot admit same-region GitHub-hosted runners).

hcpTerraform.description: HCP Terraform as a state backend only. Azure authentication is unchanged — GitHub OIDC, no stored Azure credential — so TFC never holds a credential to this tenant. It does mean one static credential the azurerm path does not have: TF_API_TOKEN, which the Terraform CLI needs to reach the workspace. Decision 0023 states that trade explicitly.

organization.description: HCP Terraform organization that owns the workspaces.

workspacePrefix.description: Workspaces are created as {prefix}-{layer}. Defaults to organization.companyShortName.

executionMode.description: Fixed. State only: Terraform runs in GitHub Actions and TFC stores the state. Remote execution is not a configuration away — the emitted plan and apply workflows gate destroys on a saved plan file (terraform plan -out=tfplan, then terraform show -json tfplan), and TFC remote runs do not support -out. Allowing remote would delete that gate from both workflows without saying so, which is why this is a const rather than an enum with a default.

acknowledgedResourceLimit.description: The HCP Terraform free tier caps managed resources under management at 500, and state-only changes nothing about that — the resources are in the state TFC holds. A full landing zone commonly exceeds it. The wizard estimates the count and requires an explicit acknowledgement before allowing hcp-terraform when the estimate is over the cap.

mode.description: greenfield: an empty-tenant assumption — new subscriptions, nothing pre-existing to consider. brownfield: pre-existing estate is RECOGNIZED and EXCLUDED, never touched (ADR 0018): new subscriptions are still created for all new deployments, excluded subscription IDs are structurally kept out of the hierarchy, and discovery inventories existing policy assignments for awareness. Integration of existing deployments is out of scope.

excludedSubscriptionIds.description: Existing subscription IDs the estate must never touch. Enforced structurally: never placed in the management-group hierarchy, never granted RBAC, and render guard G26 refuses a config that lists one of these IDs in any subscription slot.

inventoryExistingPolicies.description: Discovery records existing tenant-scope policy assignments into discovery-inventory.json and the generated governance doc, so overlap with the ALZ library is visible before first apply. Read-only.

dispositions.description: What happens to each pre-existing subscription, keyed by subscription ID. ADR 0018 made brownfield recognise-and-exclude; this is the amendment that lets a client say otherwise, per subscription, and records what they were told when they did. Governance only — no resource is ever imported into Terraform state. A subscription with no entry here is excluded, which is the safe default and the ADR 0018 behaviour.

action.description: place-now: the subscription is placed into the new management-group hierarchy on the first apply, so every ALZ policy assignment above it begins evaluating its EXISTING resources immediately. defer: the subscription stays outside the hierarchy and the factory generates written instructions for onboarding it later.

acknowledgement.description: Required for place-now, and checked against an exact expected sentence naming this subscription — render guard G30 refuses the configuration otherwise. It is deliberately not a boolean: the point is that somebody read what placing an existing subscription does to the resources already in it, and a checkbox records only that somebody clicked.

note.description: Free text carried into the generated onboarding document, for whatever the client needs to remember about this subscription.

platform.description: Platform-plane environments. Each becomes a GitHub environment, a state file, and (for hcp-terraform) a workspace.

promotionPath.description: Ordered. Must be a subsequence of application. environment-promotion.yml enforces that a change reaching stage N has succeeded at N-1.

requiredReviewers.description: GitHub logins or team slugs gating the GitHub environment.

approvals.description: Keyed by environment name from platform or application.

model.description: hub-spoke renders terraform/live/platform-connectivity using the hub-network module. virtual-wan is declared here but is NOT implemented in the current module corpus — the renderer rejects it until the module exists rather than emitting a broken layer.

nonProdSpokeAddressSpaces.description: Per-environment workload spoke CIDRs. A selected dev, test, or uat environment requires its matching entry; the renderer enforces that relationship.

type.description: Azure Firewall — the only firewall type the AVM connectivity patterns deploy (ADR 0017). This says WHICH firewall, not WHETHER: connectivity.firewall.enabled is a separate required answer that accepts false.
type.$comment: The `none` value was retired from this enum on 2026-08-30, and it did not become the `enabled` answer — it was replaced by it. Choosing not to deploy a firewall is `enabled: false`, which the AVM connectivity patterns accept; this enum only narrows the type, and palo/fortinet NVA options retired with the bespoke hub-network module (ADR 0017) because third-party NVAs are per-estate work inside the generated repository. An imported configuration still carrying type `none` is blocked by the wizard rather than silently read as `enabled: false`, since the two meant different things.

azfwTier.$comment: Basic is deliberately excluded: the hub-network module does not provision the dedicated AzureFirewallManagementSubnet (/26) and management public IP that the Basic tier mandates, and Basic only supports threat-intel alert mode while the layer defaults to Deny. A Basic selection would render a configuration that can never apply.

threatIntelligenceMode.description: Secure default is Deny. Off requires an explicit governance exception.

enabled.description: Whether the hub deploys an Azure Firewall. Deliberately has NO default: Azure Firewall Standard is roughly USD 900-950/month per hub before data processing, and a silent default is the wrong way to make an eleven-thousand-dollar-a-year decision. The AVM connectivity patterns accept false (ADR 0017, amended 2026-08-30).
Whether the hub deploys Azure Bastion. No default, for the same reason as firewall.enabled: Bastion Standard is roughly USD 140/month per hub and there may be nothing to reach through it.

zones.description: Private DNS zones to create in the connectivity subscription and link to every hub, e.g. privatelink.blob.core.windows.net. Empty means privatelink.blob.core.windows.net alone — there is no CAF default set behind this field.

enabled.description: Create private endpoints for PaaS resources. ANDs with the connectivity layer's private DNS zone — an endpoint without a matching zone resolves to nothing.

denyPublicNetworkAccessPolicy.description: Assign the public-network-access initiative (storage accounts and key vaults) over the Landing Zones management group. Ships with the Audit effect: the platform's own storage accounts rely on network rules rather than private endpoints, so Deny would fail the first apply.

cicdIdentityModel.description: Broker-only (like github.*): consumed by factory/bootstrap, never mapped to a Terraform variable, deliberately absent from factory/renderer/variable-map.json. 'minimal' (default) creates 2 Entra identities total — one shared plan identity and one shared apply identity carrying one federated credential per environment. 'per-environment' creates a plan/apply pair per unique environment (2 × N).

privilegedAccessModel.description: standing-access is recorded as a governance exception in the generated security docs.

breakGlassAccounts.description: At least two, per Microsoft guidance. Names/emails only — never credentials (see risk SR7; the schema forbids secret-typed fields entirely).

customerManagedKeys.description: Consumes the keyvault-cmk module, which is scaffold-only today. The renderer rejects true until that module is implemented rather than silently producing a no-op.

enforcementMode.description: Global default effect. Downgrading an individual policy from Deny to Audit is blocked by the policy-checks workflow (risk GR1).

requiredTags.description: Enforced by the require-tag policies in the policy-baseline module.

policyAsCodeEngines.description: sentinel was a Terraform Cloud enforcement feature and retired with the dual-backend capability (ADR 0015).

complianceFrameworks.description: Drives which built-in Azure Policy initiatives are assigned and which sections appear in the generated compliance docs.

regulatoryNotes.description: Free text reproduced verbatim into docs/governance-model.md. Not parsed.

dataResidencyRegions.description: If non-empty, allowedLocations is intersected with this set and a residency policy is assigned.

policySelection.description: Which Azure Landing Zones policy assignments this estate creates, and what they are configured with. Choices are made against site/alz-policy-catalog.json, generated from the library ref pinned in factory-version.json — so the wizard can only offer policies the deployment will actually produce. Unselected assignments are emitted as creation_enabled = false into the global layer's policy_assignments_to_modify, keyed by every management group that carries them (many are carried by more than one).

groups.description: Capability group id from the catalog -> whether that group's assignments are created. An absent group is treated as enabled, so a config written before a library bump keeps the ALZ default posture rather than silently dropping newly added policies.

creationEnabled.description: False emits creation_enabled = false for this assignment. Overrides the group setting.

enforcementMode.description: Overrides governance.policyBaseline.enforcementMode for this one assignment. Default enforces; DoNotEnforce reports compliance without acting.

assignments.description: Per-assignment overrides from the advanced list, keyed by assignment name as the catalog spells it. Takes precedence over the containing group.

ddos_protection_plan_id.description: Resource ID of an existing DDoS Network Protection plan, required when the DDoS capability group is enabled. The factory creates no plan: Enable-DDoS-VNET is a Modify effect that attaches this one to every virtual network, so a value that is not a real resource ID is written onto the estate at create and update.

email_security_contact.description: Address Microsoft Defender for Cloud notifies, required when any Defender assignment is selected. Seeded from security.defender.securityContactEmail but separately editable: an estate can send policy-driven notifications somewhere other than the contact recorded on the plan.

values.description: Policy default values that a selection obliges the client to supply, keyed by the library's default name — for example ddos_protection_plan_id when DDoS protection is enabled, or email_security_contact when any Defender assignment is. Unsupplied, the assignment would be created from the library's own placeholder (an all-zeroes subscription, or security_contact@replace_me), which is why the wizard refuses to export with an enabled group's required value blank. The two named here are the ones the emitted global layer consumes today; the open shape is what lets a library bump add another without a schema major.

dailyQuotaGb.description: -1 means no cap. Any positive value risks dropped security telemetry and is flagged in the generated observability doc.

schedule.description: Five-field cron for the scheduled drift-detection workflow, UTC.

operatingModel.description: CAF operating model. Determines default RBAC scoping in the generated governance docs: centralized keeps write access at platform MG, federated delegates at landing-zone MG, decentralized at subscription.

approvalChain.description: Ordered approval stages reproduced into docs/operating-model.md and used to seed GitHub environment reviewers.

breakGlassContacts.description: Humans reachable during an identity or OIDC outage. Distinct from identity.breakGlassAccounts, which are Entra accounts.

defaultSubscriptionBudget.description: A default budget placed on EVERY subscription beneath one management group, by assigning the pinned ALZ library's own Deploy-Budget policy. This is the one budget mechanism the factory deploys. It is deliberately not the same thing as finops.budgets: that list is per-scope and free-text, and it is recorded in docs/finops.md for someone to act on. Deploy-Budget is a DeployIfNotExists policy, so it creates the Microsoft.Consumption budget on subscriptions that exist now AND on every subscription added under the scope later — which is the property a hand-built budget resource cannot have.

enabled.description: Assign Deploy-Budget. When false nothing is emitted and the estate carries no policy-created budget.

managementGroup.description: Which management group the assignment lands on, keyed by the PINNED LIBRARY's id rather than any rename this estate applies — the rename is resolved during rendering. Every subscription beneath it gets a budget. 'alz' is the tenant root: the whole estate. Note that caf-minimal does not create sandbox or decommissioned, so selecting one of those alongside caf-minimal is refused (guard G32).

amountUsd.description: Budget amount per subscription, in the billing currency. Named Usd for consistency with finops.budgets; Azure budgets carry no currency of their own and take the billing account's.

warningThresholdPercent.description: First notification threshold, as a percentage of the amount. Deploy-Budget takes EXACTLY TWO thresholds — this one and capThresholdPercent — which is why this block does not reuse the alertThresholdPercents array finops.budgets carries.

capThresholdPercent.description: Second notification threshold, as a percentage of the amount. Must be greater than warningThresholdPercent (guard G33). Nothing is stopped at either threshold: an Azure budget notifies, it does not cap spend.

timeGrain.description: Reset period. The Billing* variants follow the billing account's cycle rather than the calendar. These are the values the Deploy-Budget definition itself allows, which is why the list is longer than the one on finops.budgets.

contactEmails.description: Addresses notified at both thresholds. May be empty, in which case contactRoles alone carries the notification.

contactRoles.description: Subscription roles notified at both thresholds, resolved per subscription at alert time. This is what makes the default budget useful without knowing every subscription's owner in advance.

standard.description: caf uses the Microsoft CAF abbreviations already documented in README.md: mg-{scope}, rg-{scope}-{region}-{env}-{nn}, {type}-{name}-{region}-{env}-{nn}.

resourceGroupPattern.description: Required when standard=custom. Supported tokens: {org} {scope} {workload} {region} {regionCode} {env} {nn}. Any other token is a render-time error, so no placeholder can silently survive into output.

resourcePattern.description: Required when standard=custom. Same token set, plus {type} for the CAF resource abbreviation.

environmentAbbreviations.description: Maps environment name to the token substituted for {env}, e.g. { "prod": "prd", "sandbox": "sbx" }.

defaultTags.description: Merged into the default_tags variable of every live layer. Keys listed in governance.policyBaseline.requiredTags must all be present here or the renderer fails — otherwise the generated deployment would be denied by its own policy on first apply.
